subject: Default storage pathways for live request streams vs post-run artifacts
messages:
From: Anna Gomez <anna.gomez@atlasretail.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: corp-security@atlasretail.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 08:13:00 -0700
Subject: Question: do streamed tokens get stored by default?

Hi Jasmine,

Quick follow-up from our security review: when we integrate Redwood for conversational search, the client will stream partial responses to users as tokens are generated. Can you confirm whether those intermediate streamed tokens (the partial stream fragments sent over the wire) are captured and stored by Redwood by default, or are they only transient in memory until the final response is assembled?

We also want to understand the default retention windows for: (1) raw request payloads (user inputs), (2) final model outputs (the completed answer), and (3) any derived artifacts (embeddings, rerank logs). Our security team is mapping retention windows for the pilot.

Thanks — if easier we can hop on a 20-min call. I attached our questionnaire (v1) with a few targeted items.

Anna Gomez
Product Manager, Atlas Retail
anna.gomez@atlasretail.com

Attachment: atlas-questionnaire-v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Anna Gomez <anna.gomez@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: do streamed tokens get stored by default?

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear questions and for sending the questionnaire. Short answer up front: intermediate streamed fragments are transient by default and are not persisted as discrete artifacts unless the session is explicitly configured to persist streams or the final output is saved. Below is a short, actionable breakdown you can share with security and engineering teams.

What we store by default (hosted Redwood API):
- Raw requests (user inputs): persisted for 30 days by default for hosted customers; retained for longer (configurable) on Dedicated or Private deployments.
- Final model outputs (completed answers): persisted for 180 days by default to support debugging, evals, and incident investigation; customers can request shorter windows or opt-out for specific routes.
- Streaming fragments / token-by-token buffers: ephemeral in-memory buffers only. We do not write these streaming fragments to long-term storage unless a customer enables session_persistence or explicitly calls the save endpoint.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, reranking scores, eval snapshots): treated as separate artifacts with their own retention class — default is 90 days for hosted. These are logged as indexed artifacts; they are included in audit exports when requested.
- KV cache contents: kept in-memory for the life of the inference session and not persisted across sessions unless configured via persistent-kv in Private deployments.

Exceptions and controls:
- Customers on Dedicated/Private can configure all retention windows via the Console or API, and can route logs to a chosen region for residency requirements.
- For EU data residency we support routing both request/response storage and audit logs to EU buckets (region=eu) — please flag in the questionnaire if you require that.
- If a customer needs zero-storage for prompts/outputs, we offer a session_persistence=false mode at the route level; note this disables some features (longer-term evals, cost-analytics).

Security/evidence: we can provide the retention diagram and a short export showing how an example chat session flows through the stack (attached). If your security team needs SOC2-aligned evidence for our default hosted behavior, I can loop in our compliance teammate.

If helpful I can schedule a quick call with Karthik to walk through configuration options and the questionnaire. Proposed times tomorrow morning PST — any preference?

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: retention-pathways-diagram.png

Quick note — looks solid. Two suggested clarifications before sending the final to Atlas:
1) Call out the default hosted retention windows explicitly in the email body (you did) but also include a one-line about audit log retention separately (audit logs retained 365 days by default for hosted; can be shortened via support ticket).
2) Add a short paragraph on encryption and access controls for stored items (at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys available on Private/Dedicated).

I added these as inline suggestions on the diagram. Happy to sign off once Jasmine updates.

—Kim

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Anna Gomez <anna.gomez@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: do streamed tokens get stored by default?

Hi Anna — following up with the finalized notes and attachments. Key points for Atlas Retail:
- Streamed tokens: ephemeral by default (never persisted unless session_persistence is toggled on).
- Default hosted retention windows: requests = 30 days; final outputs = 180 days; derived artifacts = 90 days; audit logs = 365 days.
- Residency: can pin storage and audit exports to eu/us/apac via Console settings; Dedicated/Private give full control.
- Opt-outs: route-level session_persistence=false or portal request to disable storage for specific endpoints.

Next steps if you want us to produce formal evidence: we can (A) provide a short export demonstrating the lifecycle for one test session, (B) deliver our retention policy excerpt for your security binder, and/or (C) schedule a 20-min call with Karthik for config walkthrough. What would you prefer?

Thanks — attaching the diagram and the annotated questionnaire.

Jasmine
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com

Attachments: retention-pathways-diagram.png; atlas-questionnaire-v1.xlsx
